spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m4p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

Deadbolts == {"front", "patio"}
MaxEpoch == 2
Cap == 2

VARIABLES queue, epoch, current, mode, override

vars == <<queue, epoch, current, mode, override>>

Modes == {"closed", "resident", "admin"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Deadbolts)
    /\ Len(queue) <= Cap
    /\ epoch \in [Deadbolts -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ current \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ mode \in [Deadbolts -> Modes]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ epoch = [d \in Deadbolts |-> 0]
    /\ current = 0
    /\ mode = [d \in Deadbolts |-> "closed"]
    /\ override = FALSE

Submit(d) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ epoch[d] = current
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, d)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, current, mode, override>>

Apply ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET d == Head(queue) IN
         /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "resident"]
         /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, current, override>>

Rotate ==
    /\ current < MaxEpoch
    /\ current' = current + 1
    /\ queue' = << >>
    /\ mode' = [d \in Deadbolts |->
                  IF mode[d] = "resident" THEN "closed" ELSE mode[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override>>

Refresh(d) ==
    /\ epoch[d] # current
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![d] = current]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, current, mode, override>>

ArmOverride ==
    /\ override = FALSE
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch, current, mode>>

DisarmOverride ==
    /\ override = TRUE
    /\ \A d \in Deadbolts : mode[d] # "admin"
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch, current, mode>>

AdminOpen(d) ==
    /\ override = TRUE
    /\ mode[d] = "closed"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "admin"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch, current, override>>

Close(d) ==
    /\ mode[d] # "closed"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "closed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch, current, override>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Deadbolts : Submit(d)
    \/ Apply
    \/ Rotate
    \/ \E d \in Deadbolts : Refresh(d)
    \/ ArmOverride
    \/ DisarmOverride
    \/ \E d \in Deadbolts : AdminOpen(d)
    \/ \E d \in Deadbolts : Close(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction ==
    /\ Len(queue) <= Cap
    /\ \A i \in 1..Len(queue) : epoch[queue[i]] = current
    /\ \A d \in Deadbolts : mode[d] = "resident" => epoch[d] = current
    /\ \A d \in Deadbolts : mode[d] = "admin" => override = TRUE
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TypeOK
INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction
nl:
A smart-home door lock network connects several battery-powered deadbolts to a single hub. Each deadbolt holds a credential stamped with an epoch number, and the hub keeps the epoch it currently considers valid. When a resident triggers a lock or unlock at a deadbolt, the hub does not act immediately: the request is appended to a bounded work queue, and the queue applies backpressure, refusing new requests once it is full. The hub drains the queue one request at a time, and applying a request unlocks that deadbolt in resident mode.

Because a credential can be leaked, the installer can rotate the hub's epoch at any time. Rotation is a lockdown event: every request still waiting in the queue is discarded, and every deadbolt that was standing open in resident mode is relocked, because those grants were made against a credential that is no longer trusted. A deadbolt catches up by refreshing its credential to the hub's current epoch, after which it may submit requests again.

Separately, a privileged installer override lets a deadbolt be opened in admin mode with no queue and no credential check at all. The override switch must be armed before any admin-mode opening can occur. Any open deadbolt, resident or admin, can be closed again at any time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The queue never exceeds its capacity and never holds a request from a deadbolt whose credential epoch differs from the hub's current epoch, no deadbolt stands open in resident mode unless its credential still matches the hub's current epoch, and no deadbolt is open in admin mode unless the installer override is armed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m0p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Banks == {"nordbank", "sudbank"}
Capacity == 2
MaxVersion == 3
NoRead == 0-1
Empty == "empty"
Slots == 1..Capacity

VARIABLES batch, version, snap, alive, cut

vars == <<batch, version, snap, alive, cut>>

FreeSlots == {i \in Slots : batch[i] = Empty}

TypeOK ==
    /\ batch \in [Slots -> Banks \cup {Empty}]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ snap \in [Banks -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ alive \in [Banks -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ cut \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ batch = [i \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [b \in Banks |-> NoRead]
    /\ alive = [b \in Banks |-> TRUE]
    /\ cut = FALSE

ReadRecord(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ snap[b] = NoRead
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, version, alive, cut>>

Commit(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ cut = FALSE
    /\ snap[b] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ FreeSlots # {}
    /\ LET first == CHOOSE i \in FreeSlots :
                       \A j \in FreeSlots : i <= j
       IN batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![first] = b]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, cut>>

Retry(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ snap[b] # NoRead
    /\ snap[b] # version
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, version, alive, cut>>

CutBatch ==
    /\ cut = FALSE
    /\ cut' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, version, snap, alive>>

Settle ==
    /\ cut = TRUE
    /\ batch' = [i \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ version' = 0
    /\ cut' = FALSE
    /\ snap' = [b \in Banks |-> NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

Crash(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, version, cut>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : ReadRecord(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Commit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Retry(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Crash(b)
    \/ CutBatch
    \/ Settle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BatchCapacityRespected ==
    /\ \A i \in Slots :
         batch[i] = Empty => \A j \in Slots : (j >= i => batch[j] = Empty)
    /\ \A b \in Banks : ~alive[b] => snap[b] = NoRead
    /\ \A b \in Banks : snap[b] # NoRead => snap[b] <= version
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BatchCapacityRespected
nl:
Two member banks post payment entries into a shared interbank settlement batch held at the clearing house. The batch record carries a version stamp and can hold at most a fixed number of entries before it must be cut and sent for settlement. There are no locks: a bank first reads the batch record, remembering the version stamp it saw, then later tries to commit its entry. The commit succeeds only if the version stamp is still exactly what the bank read; the clearing house then adds the entry and bumps the version. If another bank committed in between, the stamp no longer matches and the first bank must abandon its read and retry from scratch.

The clearing house can cut the batch, which closes it to further commits, and can then settle it, emptying the batch, bumping the version and reopening it for the next cycle.

A member bank can crash silently at any moment. It simply stops participating, and whatever read it was holding is dropped on the floor rather than lingering as a phantom claim on the batch. A crashed bank never reads, commits or retries again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The batch never holds more entries than its capacity, no entry is ever added to a batch that has been cut, and no bank holds an outstanding read unless it is still alive and that read's version stamp is no newer than the clearing house's current version.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m5p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Firms == {"altair", "borea"}
Slots == 1..2
Quorum == 2
None == "none"

VARIABLES prop, tally, owner, width, session

vars == <<prop, tally, owner, width, session>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ prop \in [Slots -> Firms \cup {None}]
    /\ tally \in [Slots -> 0..Quorum]
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Firms \cup {None}]
    /\ width \in Slots
    /\ session \in {"auction", "continuous"}

Init ==
    /\ prop = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ tally = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ width = 2
    /\ session = "auction"

FileProposal(s, f) ==
    /\ session = "auction"
    /\ s <= width
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ prop[s] = None
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![s] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, owner, width, session>>

CastVote(s) ==
    /\ prop[s] # None
    /\ tally[s] < Quorum
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = tally[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, owner, width, session>>

CommitAllocation(s) ==
    /\ prop[s] # None
    /\ tally[s] >= Quorum
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = prop[s]]
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<width, session>>

Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ prop[s] # None
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, width, session>>

Resize(w) ==
    /\ session = "auction"
    /\ w \in Slots
    /\ w # width
    /\ \A s \in Slots : (s > w => (owner[s] = None /\ prop[s] = None))
    /\ width' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, tally, owner, session>>

Cross ==
    /\ session = "auction"
    /\ \A s \in Slots : prop[s] = None
    /\ session' = "continuous"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, tally, owner, width>>

Reopen ==
    /\ session = "continuous"
    /\ owner' = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ session' = "auction"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, tally, width>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, f \in Firms : FileProposal(s, f)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : CastVote(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : CommitAllocation(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E w \in Slots : Resize(w)
    \/ Cross
    \/ Reopen

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : ~(owner[s] # None /\ prop[s] # None)
    /\ \A s \in Slots : prop[s] = None => tally[s] = 0
    /\ \A s \in Slots : s > width => (owner[s] = None /\ prop[s] = None)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
Before the regular session begins, the exchange runs an opening auction in which member firms are allocated price-discovery slots. Allocation is not unilateral: a firm first files a proposal for a particular slot, and the surveillance committee then votes on it. Each vote is tallied against that proposal, and only once the tally reaches the required quorum may the exchange commit the allocation, at which point the slot's owner is fixed and the proposal and its tally are cleared. A proposal that is losing support can be withdrawn instead, which also clears its tally.

A slot that already has an owner is closed for business: no new proposal may be filed against it, so it cannot be handed to a second firm.

The number of slots actually in service is not fixed. The exchange can widen or narrow the auction at runtime as volatility dictates. Narrowing is only permitted down to a width that still covers every slot that is already allocated or has a live proposal; slots above the current width carry neither an owner nor a proposal.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot ever carries both an owner and a live proposal, no tally exists without the proposal it counts votes for, and no slot beyond the auction's current width is allocated or under proposal.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m3p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Cabinets == {"cab1", "cab2"}
Blocks == 1..2
MaxTerm == 2
NoLeader == "noleader"
Ungranted == "ungranted"

VARIABLES leader, term, healthy, holder, gterm, inService

vars == <<leader, term, healthy, holder, gterm, inService>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Cabinets \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ healthy \in [Cabinets -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ holder \in [Blocks -> Cabinets \cup {Ungranted}]
    /\ gterm \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ inService \in Blocks

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ term = 0
    /\ healthy = [c \in Cabinets |-> TRUE]
    /\ holder = [b \in Blocks |-> Ungranted]
    /\ gterm = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ inService = 2

StandForElection(c) ==
    /\ healthy[c]
    /\ c # leader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ holder' = [b \in Blocks |-> Ungranted]
    /\ gterm' = [b \in Blocks |-> term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<healthy, inService>>

IssueGrant(b) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ healthy[leader]
    /\ b <= inService
    /\ holder[b] = Ungranted
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = leader]
    /\ gterm' = [gterm EXCEPT ![b] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, inService>>

ClearBlock(b) ==
    /\ holder[b] # Ungranted
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = Ungranted]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, gterm, inService>>

CabinetFails(c) ==
    /\ healthy[c]
    /\ healthy' = [healthy EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ holder' = [b \in Blocks |->
                    IF holder[b] = c THEN Ungranted ELSE holder[b]]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = c THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, gterm, inService>>

Reconfigure(n) ==
    /\ n \in Blocks
    /\ n # inService
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : (b > n => holder[b] = Ungranted)
    /\ inService' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, holder, gterm>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cabinets : StandForElection(c)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : IssueGrant(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : ClearBlock(b)
    \/ \E c \in Cabinets : CabinetFails(c)
    \/ \E n \in Blocks : Reconfigure(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

GrantsAreCurrentAndAuthorized ==
    \A b \in Blocks :
        holder[b] # Ungranted =>
            /\ holder[b] = leader
            /\ gterm[b] = term
            /\ healthy[holder[b]]
            /\ b <= inService
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT GrantsAreCurrentAndAuthorized
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and trains may only enter a block that has been granted to them by the line controller. Several controller cabinets stand ready, but exactly one of them is the elected leader at any moment, and each election carries a term number that strictly increases. When the current leader's cabinet fails, a surviving cabinet stands for election in a new term and takes over.

Failover is deliberately destructive to routing state. Standing on a new term revokes every block grant issued under the old term, because a grant made by a cabinet that is no longer in charge cannot be trusted to reflect where the trains actually are. After the new leader is elected it re-issues grants from scratch, stamping each one with its own term. Grants are released when the train clears the block.

The number of blocks in service changes at runtime as engineering works take track out of use or hand it back. Blocks are only taken out of service when they carry no grant.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block that currently carries a grant was granted by the cabinet that is still the leader, under the term that is still current, by a cabinet that has not failed, and lies within the stretch of line currently in service.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m8p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Swarms == {"forest", "county"}
Sectors == 1..2
MaxEpoch == 2
Free == "free"

VARIABLES perimeter, sector, auth, epoch

vars == <<perimeter, sector, auth, epoch>>

Holds(s) == perimeter = s \/ (\E k \in Sectors : sector[k] = s)

TypeOK ==
    /\ perimeter \in Swarms \cup {Free}
    /\ sector \in [Sectors -> Swarms \cup {Free}]
    /\ auth \in [Swarms -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ perimeter = Free
    /\ sector = [k \in Sectors |-> Free]
    /\ auth = [s \in Swarms |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0

TakePerimeter(s) ==
    /\ perimeter = Free
    /\ auth[s] = epoch
    /\ perimeter' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, auth, epoch>>

TakeSector(s, k) ==
    /\ perimeter = s
    /\ auth[s] = epoch
    /\ sector[k] = Free
    /\ sector' = [sector EXCEPT ![k] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<perimeter, auth, epoch>>

Surveyed(k) ==
    /\ sector[k] # Free
    /\ sector' = [sector EXCEPT ![k] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<perimeter, auth, epoch>>

DropPerimeter(s) ==
    /\ perimeter = s
    /\ \A k \in Sectors : sector[k] # s
    /\ perimeter' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, auth, epoch>>

AdvanceEpoch ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ perimeter' = IF perimeter # Free /\ auth[perimeter] # epoch + 1
                      THEN Free ELSE perimeter
    /\ sector' = [k \in Sectors |->
                    IF sector[k] # Free /\ auth[sector[k]] # epoch + 1
                      THEN Free ELSE sector[k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED auth

Renew(s) ==
    /\ auth[s] # epoch
    /\ ~Holds(s)
    /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<perimeter, sector, epoch>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Swarms : TakePerimeter(s)
    \/ \E s \in Swarms, k \in Sectors : TakeSector(s, k)
    \/ \E k \in Sectors : Surveyed(k)
    \/ \E s \in Swarms : DropPerimeter(s)
    \/ AdvanceEpoch
    \/ \E s \in Swarms : Renew(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

HierarchyAndAuthorisation ==
    /\ \A k \in Sectors : sector[k] # Free => sector[k] = perimeter
    /\ \A k \in Sectors : sector[k] # Free => auth[sector[k]] = epoch
    /\ (perimeter # Free => auth[perimeter] = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT HierarchyAndAuthorisation
nl:
Two independently operated drone swarms, one flown by the forest service and one by the county, share a single pool of airspace sectors over a wildfire. To keep them apart, the airspace is locked hierarchically: a swarm must first take the coarse lock on the whole fire perimeter, and only then may it take fine locks on individual sectors inside that perimeter. Fine locks are dropped as each sector is surveyed, and the coarse lock can only be given up once the swarm holds no fine locks at all.

Every swarm flies under a mission authorisation stamped with an epoch. The incident commander can invalidate authorisations by advancing the epoch, for instance when the fire jumps a ridge and the whole plan is redrawn. Advancing the epoch is a hard stop: any swarm still flying on the old epoch immediately loses the coarse lock and every fine lock it held, because a swarm operating on a withdrawn authorisation must not be holding airspace. A swarm returns to service by renewing its authorisation to the current epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A sector is only ever locked by the swarm that also holds the coarse perimeter lock, and no swarm holds the coarse lock or any sector lock unless its mission authorisation is stamped with the epoch that is currently in force.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m3p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Nodes == {"ctlA", "ctlB"}
Machines == 1..2
MaxTerm == 2
NoLeader == "noleader"

VARIABLES leader, term, healthy, phase, stamp, inService

vars == <<leader, term, healthy, phase, stamp, inService>>

Phases == {"idle", "authorised", "dispensed"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ healthy \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ phase \in [Machines -> Phases]
    /\ stamp \in [Machines -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ inService \in Machines

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ term = 0
    /\ healthy = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ phase = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]
    /\ stamp = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ inService = 2

StandForElection(n) ==
    /\ healthy[n]
    /\ n # leader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ phase' = [m \in Machines |->
                   IF phase[m] = "authorised" THEN "idle" ELSE phase[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<healthy, stamp, inService>>

Authorise(m) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ healthy[leader]
    /\ m <= inService
    /\ phase[m] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "authorised"]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![m] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, inService>>

Dispense(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "authorised"
    /\ stamp[m] = term
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "dispensed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, stamp, inService>>

NodeFails(n) ==
    /\ healthy[n]
    /\ healthy' = [healthy EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ phase' = IF leader = n
                  THEN [m \in Machines |->
                          IF phase[m] = "authorised" THEN "idle" ELSE phase[m]]
                  ELSE phase
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stamp, inService>>

Reconfigure(k) ==
    /\ k \in Machines
    /\ k # inService
    /\ \A m \in Machines : (m > k => phase[m] # "authorised")
    /\ inService' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, healthy, phase, stamp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : StandForElection(n)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Authorise(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Dispense(m)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : NodeFails(n)
    \/ \E k \in Machines : Reconfigure(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispenseAuthorisedAtMostOnce ==
    /\ \A m \in Machines :
         phase[m] = "authorised" =>
            /\ leader # NoLeader
            /\ healthy[leader]
            /\ stamp[m] = term
            /\ m <= inService
    /\ \A m \in Machines : phase[m] = "dispensed" => stamp[m] <= term
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAuthorisedAtMostOnce
nl:
A chain of vending machines in a campus network is driven by a regional controller. Several controller nodes are available, but only one is the elected leader at a time, and each election raises the term number. A machine will not drop product on its own: it must first receive an authorisation from the leader, stamped with the term the leader is serving, and only then may it dispense.

Dispensing is irreversible. Once a machine has dropped the product and charged the card, that order is finished for good; the machine's order never returns to an authorised state, so the same authorisation can never cause a second drop.

Failover is the interesting case. If the leading node fails, a healthy node stands for election in a fresh term, and standing voids every authorisation that has not yet been acted on, returning those machines to idle, since an authorisation from a controller that is no longer in charge must not be honoured. Orders that already dispensed are untouched by failover, because the product is gone and the card is charged.

The number of machines in service changes at runtime as sites are added or pulled from the network, and a machine is only pulled while it holds no live authorisation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A machine holds a live authorisation only if the leader that issued it is still elected and healthy, the authorisation carries the current term, and the machine is still in service; and a machine that has already dispensed carries an authorisation stamp no newer than the current term and never reverts to being authorised.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m9p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Drones == {"alpha1", "bravo1"}
Pads == 1..2
MaxEpoch == 2
Unassigned == "unassigned"
NoPad == 0

VARIABLES padBook, droneBook, padEpoch, epoch, phase

vars == <<padBook, droneBook, padEpoch, epoch, phase>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ padBook \in [Pads -> Drones \cup {Unassigned}]
    /\ droneBook \in [Drones -> Pads \cup {NoPad}]
    /\ padEpoch \in [Pads -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ phase \in {"settled", "reconfiguring"}

Init ==
    /\ padBook = [p \in Pads |-> Unassigned]
    /\ droneBook = [d \in Drones |-> NoPad]
    /\ padEpoch = [p \in Pads |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ phase = "settled"

HandOut(p, d) ==
    /\ phase = "settled"
    /\ padBook[p] = Unassigned
    /\ droneBook[d] = NoPad
    /\ padBook' = [padBook EXCEPT ![p] = d]
    /\ droneBook' = [droneBook EXCEPT ![d] = p]
    /\ padEpoch' = [padEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, phase>>

ReleasePad(d) ==
    /\ droneBook[d] # NoPad
    /\ padBook' = [padBook EXCEPT ![droneBook[d]] = Unassigned]
    /\ droneBook' = [droneBook EXCEPT ![d] = NoPad]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<padEpoch, epoch, phase>>

BeginReconfiguration ==
    /\ phase = "settled"
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ phase' = "reconfiguring"
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ padBook' = [p \in Pads |-> Unassigned]
    /\ droneBook' = [d \in Drones |-> NoPad]
    /\ UNCHANGED padEpoch

RewirePad(p) ==
    /\ phase = "reconfiguring"
    /\ padEpoch[p] # epoch
    /\ padEpoch' = [padEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]

nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder. The amount of load currently shed is held in a single register at the control centre, and the register carries a version counter that ticks on every successful write. Substation agents do not write the register directly. An agent reads the version, then sends a compare-and-swap command carrying the version it expects and the shed level it wants. The command travels over the grid's telemetry bus, which does not preserve order: commands from different agents arrive in any order, and each agent keeps at most one command outstanding.

When a command finally arrives, the control centre applies it only if the version it expects is still the register's current version; otherwise some other agent got there first and the command is discarded so the agent can re-read and try again.

Agents also carry an operating certificate. The control centre can revoke all certificates at once, for instance after a protection scheme is re-armed. Revocation flushes the telemetry bus of every command whose sender is no longer certified, so a command from a decertified agent can never land, and the centre records which agent last wrote the register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every command outstanding on the telemetry bus comes from an agent whose certificate matches the one the control centre currently recognises and expects a register version that has already been issued, and the register records a last writer whenever it has been written at all.

nl:
Three branch libraries share one reservation ledger for a rare book. To keep their edits from colliding, the branches are wired in a token ring: a single token circulates from branch to branch in a fixed order, and only the branch currently holding the token may enter the ledger and change who has the book reserved. A branch leaves the ledger before it passes the token on, so the token never travels while an edit is in progress.

Branches can crash silently. A crashed branch stops answering, stops editing and drops any reservation it was holding for a patron. If the branch that crashed happened to be carrying the token, the token is lost with it, and the ring stalls until the head office notices. The head office may then regenerate a fresh token and hand it to a living branch, but only once the branch that was carrying the old token is confirmed dead, so that two tokens can never be in circulation at the same time. A crashed branch can be rebooted later, and it comes back without a token; the branch that took the token down with it stays offline until a fresh token has been issued.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A branch is inside the ledger only while it is the branch holding the token, no crashed branch holds the token or sits inside the ledger, and the token is missing only when the branch that last carried it is dead.

nl:
A network of vending machines is maintained by roving technicians. Before touching a machine a technician takes out a lease on it from the depot, and the lease carries an expiry time measured against the depot's clock. With the override key armed, the supervisor can seize any machine outright, which tears down whatever lease was on it, and no lease can be taken out on a machine while it is seized. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every lease that still names a technician has an expiry strictly later than the depot clock, no machine is both leased and seized, and no machine is seized unless the supervisor's override key is armed.

nl:
An airport allocates its single active runway through one shared assignment register at the tower. The register names the flight that currently owns the runway, or nothing, and carries a version that ticks on every change. Controllers never overwrite the register blindly. A controller first reads the register and remembers the version it saw, then submits a compare-and-swap: the claim lands only if the version is still the one it read, otherwise the controller re-reads and tries again.

Issuing a takeoff clearance is the irreversible step. Once the flight that owns the runway is cleared, the aircraft rolls and there is no taking it back: the flight is recorded as cleared for good, the register is freed and its version ticks. A flight that has already been cleared can never own the runway again, so the same flight cannot be cleared a second time.

The duty supervisor holds an override. With the override armed, the supervisor can plant a flight straight into the register without any compare-and-swap, which is recorded as a forced assignment.

Only a robot with a live lease may be assigned a tote to ship, and the assignment is torn up if the robot's lease dies. In the opening auction the exchange admits blocks of orders into an auction book that holds a strictly limited number of lots. Admission is agreed by two-phase commit between the exchange, the clearing member and the risk desk. A round starts by proposing a block of a given size; the block is only proposed if the book has room for all of it. Each party then votes once. A unanimous yes commits the round and the block is written into the book, taking its lots; a single no aborts the round, and either way the round is wound back to idle with the votes cleared and no block proposed. Once the auction crosses, the book is emptied for the continuous session.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots in the book never exceed the book's current capacity, a round only reaches the committed state with a unanimous yes and a proposed block that still fits in the remaining room, and while the exchange is idle no block is proposed and no votes are standing.

An engine that wants to work on individual partitions must first register an intent on the whole book; only with that intent registered may it take a partition, and it may only run the cross on a partition it holds. NEXT Step
INVARIANT BerthClaimedOnce
nl:
A subway terminus allocates platform berths through one cell per berth in the dispatcher's shared memory. Each cell names the train occupying the berth, or nothing, and carries a stamp that ticks on every change: a berth that has been claimed always sits on an odd stamp, and a berth that has been given back sits on an even one. Dispatchers never write a cell blindly. A dispatcher reads a berth's cell, remembering the stamp it saw, and then submits a compare-and-swap claim; the claim lands only if the stamp is still what it read, so two dispatchers racing for the same berth cannot both win it. A dispatcher whose stamp has gone stale throws its read away and starts again. A berth is given back when the train departs, which ticks the stamp again.

A berth is only taken out of service while it is empty, and no claim may be made on a berth that is out of service. When every berth is empty and the stamps have run to the end of their range, the dispatcher's memory is re-based for the next service day.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A berth is occupied exactly when its stamp is odd, no berth out of service is occupied, and no dispatcher holds a read whose stamp is newer than the berth cell it read.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, exclusive, badge, shift, rowsOpen>>

UnlockRow(r) ==
    /\ rowLock[r] # Unlocked
    /\ rowLock' = [rowLock EXCEPT ![r] = Unlocked]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, exclusive, badge, shift, rowsOpen>>

LeaveBay(c) ==
    /\ admitted[c]
    /\ ~HoldsRow(c)
    /\ admitted' = [admitted EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ exclusive' = IF exclusive = c THEN Vacant ELSE exclusive
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rowLock, badge, shift, rowsOpen>>

ShiftChange ==
    /\ shift < MaxShift
    /\ shift' = shift + 1
    /\ admitted' = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ rowLock' = [r \in Rows |-> Unlocked]
    /\ exclusive' = Vacant
    /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, rowsOpen>>

SignOn(c) ==
    /\ badge[c] # shift
    /\ ~admitted[c]
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![c] = shift]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, exclusive, rowLock, shift, rowsOpen>>

Replan(n) ==
    /\ n \in Rows
    /\ n # rowsOpen
    /\ \A r \in Rows : (r > n => rowLock[r] = Unlocked)
    /\ rowsOpen' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, exclusive, rowLock, badge, shift>>

Step ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : AdmitShared(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : AdmitExclusive(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, r \in Rows : LockRow(c, r)
    \/ \E r \in Rows : UnlockRow(r)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : LeaveBay(c)
    \/ ShiftChange
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : SignOn(c)
    \/ \E n \in Rows : Replan(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Step]_vars

YardAccessDiscipline ==
    /\ \A r \in Rows : rowLock[r] # Unlocked => admitted[rowLock[r]]
    /\ \A c \in Cranes : admitted[c] => badge[c] = shift
    /\ (exclusive # Vacant =>
          /\ admitted[exclusive]
          /\ \A c \in Cranes : admitted[c] => c = exclusive)
    /\ \A r \in Rows : r > rowsOpen => rowLock[r] = Unlocked

INIT Init
NEXT Step
INVARIANT YardAccessDiscipline
nl:
A container terminal runs its gantry cranes over a yard organised as a bay containing rows. Access is locked at two levels. A crane must first be admitted to the bay, and only then may it lock an individual row. Admission comes in two flavours: several cranes can be admitted to the bay together for ordinary shared working, or a single crane can be admitted exclusively for a heavy lift, which is only granted when no other crane is in the bay at all. A crane leaves the bay only after it has released every row it holds.

Every crane driver signs on with a shift badge, and the yard office runs a shift change by advancing the shift number. A shift change is a hard stop for anyone still on an old badge: a crane whose badge is from a previous shift is thrown out of the bay and loses every row it holds, and if the exclusive slot belonged to such a crane, that slot falls vacant too. A driver returns to work by signing on for the current shift, which is only possible while off the bay.

The number of rows in service changes at runtime as stacks are re-planned. A row is only taken out of service while it is unlocked, and no row out of service may be locked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every locked row belongs to a crane that is currently admitted to the bay, every crane admitted to the bay carries a badge for the current shift, whenever the bay is held exclusively the exclusive crane is the only crane admitted, and no row out of service is locked.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Positions == {"north", "south"}
Runways == 1..2
MaxEpoch == 2
Unheld == "unheld"
NoOverride == "nooverride"

VARIABLES epoch, planState, loaded, assignment, overrideFor

vars == <<epoch, planState, loaded, assignment, overrideFor>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ planState \in {"inForce", "installing"}
    /\ loaded \in [Positions -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ assignment \in [Runways -> Positions \cup {Unheld}]
    /\ overrideFor \in Positions \cup {NoOverride}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ planState = "inForce"
    /\ loaded = [p \in Positions |-> 0]
    /\ assignment = [r \in Runways |-> Unheld]
    /\ overrideFor = NoOverride

BeginInstallation ==
    /\ planState = "inForce"
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ planState' = "installing"
    /\ assignment' = [r \in Runways |-> Unheld]
    /\ overrideFor' = NoOverride
    /\ UNCHANGED loaded

LoadPlan(p) ==
    /\ loaded[p] # epoch
    /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, assignment, overrideFor>>

CompleteInstallation ==
    /\ planState = "installing"
    /\ \A p \in Positions : loaded[p] = epoch
    /\ planState' = "inForce"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, loaded, assignment, overrideFor>>

AssignRunway(p, r) ==
    /\ planState = "inForce"
    /\ loaded[p] = epoch
    /\ assignment[r] = Unheld
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, loaded, overrideFor>>

NameOverride(p) ==
    /\ planState = "installing"
    /\ overrideFor = NoOverride
    /\ loaded[p] = epoch
    /\ overrideFor' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, loaded, assignment>>

AssignUnderOverride(r) ==
    /\ planState = "installing"
    /\ overrideFor # NoOverride
    /\ loaded[overrideFor] = epoch
    /\ assignment[r] = Unheld
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![r] = overrideFor]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, loaded, overrideFor>>

WithdrawOverride ==
    /\ overrideFor # NoOverride
    /\ assignment' = [r \in Runways |->
                        IF assignment[r] = overrideFor /\ planState = "installing"
                          THEN Unheld ELSE assignment[r]]
    /\ overrideFor' = NoOverride
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, loaded>>

ReleaseRunway(r) ==
    /\ assignment[r] # Unheld
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![r] = Unheld]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, planState, loaded, overrideFor>>

Step ==
    \/ BeginInstallation
    \/ \E p \in Positions : LoadPlan(p)
    \/ CompleteInstallation
    \/ \E p \in Positions, r \in Runways : AssignRunway(p, r)
    \/ \E p \in Positions : NameOverride(p)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : AssignUnderOverride(r)
    \/ WithdrawOverride
    \/ \E r \in Runways : ReleaseRunway(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Step]_vars

OnlyCurrentPositionsHoldRunways ==
    /\ \A r \in Runways :
         assignment[r] # Unheld => loaded[assignment[r]] = epoch
    /\ (planState = "installing" =>
          \A r \in Runways :
            assignment[r] # Unheld => assignment[r] = overrideFor)
    /\ (overrideFor # NoOverride => loaded[overrideFor] = epoch)
    /\ (planState = "inForce" => \A p \in Positions : loaded[p] = epoch)
====

INVARIANT OnlyCurrentPositionsHoldRunways
nl:
A runway allocator distributes runways to controller positions, and the airspace plan it works from is versioned by an epoch number. Every controller position carries the epoch of the plan it has loaded. Only a controller whose loaded epoch matches the plan currently in force may hold a runway assignment.

Re-planning starts an installation: the epoch advances, every runway assignment standing under the old plan is withdrawn, and each controller must load the new plan before it counts as current again. The installation is declared complete only once every position has loaded the new epoch, and ordinary assignments resume only after that.

There is one privileged exception. The watch supervisor can name a single controller as the override position, which lets that one controller keep allocating runways while the installation is still in progress; the supervisor may only name a controller that has already loaded the new plan. The override can be withdrawn at any time, and while an installation is in progress no runway may be held by anyone other than the named override position.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway assignment is held by a controller whose loaded epoch is the one in force; while an installation is in progress the only controller holding a runway is the named override position, and that position has itself loaded the epoch in force; and once an installation is complete every controller has loaded the epoch in force.
